chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, who said: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, from his father, who said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'And celebrate (constantly) the praises of thy Lord, before the rising of the sun, and before its setting;' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is incumbent upon every Muslim to say, before the rising of the sun ten times, and before its setting ten times: "There is no god but God. There is no partner for Him. To Him belongs the Rule and praise is for Him. He revives and deadens. He is the Living Who never dies. All good is done by His Hand. And He is the One who is able to do everything."' I said: 'There is no god but God. There is no partner for Him. To Him belongs the Rule and praise is for Him. He revives and deadens, and deadens and revives.' He said: 'O man, there is no doubt that Allah revives and deadens, and deadens and revives, but say as I say.'

key_terms.قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: Before the rising of the sun

ai.seo_question: What is the specific dhikr and method prescribed for the verse 'Before the rising of the sun and before its setting'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the Quranic command to glorify God before sunrise and sunset as a specific ritual obligation (fard) requiring the recitation of a precise dhikr ten times at each time. The Imam emphasizes the theological precision of the phrase 'He revives and deadens' (yuhyi wa yumitu), noting that while the reverse order is not incorrect, the specific wording he dictates is the preferred form of worship. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the exact phrasing transmitted from the Imams for specific devotional acts.
